transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I keep going over the same worries about getting some detail wrong in my project, and it’s crowding out everything else in my day. It just feels like my mind won't let it go, and it's becoming really exhausting.

When these worries come up, do you feel driven to do anything repeatedly to reduce the anxiety, like checking, counting, or mentally reviewing things over and over? Or is it more a constant stream of worry about many different things?

Yes, I definitely feel driven to do those things to calm myself down. I find myself re-reading paragraphs in my grant proposal, re-measuring label placements repeatedly until it feels "just right," and whispering facts under my breath like a checklist. On top of that, I'm constantly combing through the exhibit details in my head, replaying everything over and over again.
Do these repeated checking, re-reading, or mental rituals feel unwanted and hard to control, even though you know they are excessive or not really necessary?

Yes, they feel completely unwanted and out of my control. Even though I know I've already checked things a dozen times and that it's excessive, I still feel this overwhelming urge to keep re-reading or mentally reviewing until it feels "just right." It is incredibly exhausting to realize how unmanageable these habits have become.
Do you recognize these thoughts and repeated actions as your own unwanted obsessions/compulsions, and do you feel they are excessive even while you feel unable to stop?

Yes, I definitely recognize them as my own thoughts, and I know intellectually that continuing to check is completely illogical since I've already done it multiple times. Yet, I still feel this uncontrollable urge to repeat these actions and just can't seem to stop myself. It has made me realize that these habits have become completely unmanageable.
How much time do these worries and repeated checking take up each day, and are they interfering with your work, relationships, or daily activities?

They take up a huge portion of my day, even when I'm just trying to eat dinner or watch TV. Because these checking loops consume so much of my time and energy, I've missed internal deadlines on my museum commission, turned down smaller jobs, and started skipping church and guild events.

Do you also have any rituals or checking that you do to prevent something bad from happening, or is it mainly the need to make things feel 'just right'? How much time per day do these behaviors usually take?

It’s a mix of both—I do these checks to prevent making a mistake that might disrespect the story or misquote someone, but I also have to keep repeating them until it feels "just right." These rituals consume almost my entire day, constantly interrupting normal things like eating dinner and taking up so much time that I've missed deadlines and skipped church events.
Do you ever feel that these repeated checking or mental rituals are unreasonable or excessive, even while you still feel unable to stop them?

Yes, I absolutely feel they are unreasonable and excessive. Logically, I know I've already checked the details a dozen times and nothing has changed, but I still feel this overwhelming, uncontrollable urge to keep repeating the checks until they feel "just right." Even when I am completely exhausted, I just can't seem to stop.

final_diagnosis.reason: The interview is most consistent with obsessive-compulsive disorder: the patient has intrusive, repetitive doubts about details being wrong, and performs time-consuming compulsions/mental rituals (re-reading, repeated measuring, whispering/checklist-like reviewing, mental replaying) that are recognized as excessive, unwanted, and difficult to control. Symptoms occupy much of the day and cause clear functional impairment at work and in social/religious activities.
